Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 service and eight trial days back

Last month I told Dana I would report back on Harbor Point once my writer had been through a real trial. It has now come through eight days of a civil trial, so here is the promised review.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, and picked it up Tuesday, October 27: six business days against the ten quoted. The estimate was $285 for a full recalibration, number bar sensor inspection, cleaning and firmware update. The completed work included full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning and an update from firmware 4.0.7 to 4.2.1.

The final bill was $310, including an approved $25 battery replacement. Gloria emailed on October 22 to say the internal battery was holding about 60 percent of its rated capacity and to ask whether I wanted it replaced. She specifically said she would not proceed without approval. I said yes. I appreciate being asked rather than finding an extra charge at pickup, and I think $310 was fair for the work done. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment; there was no reimbursement from the court. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The important part is how it writes. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. After eight trial days, I am satisfied with the repair and recalibration. That is a useful working test, though it is not a claim about how the machine will behave six months from now.

It also came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before. It is a small thing, but it gives me a record of what was actually done instead of leaving me to rely on “all checked out.”

A loaner was provided, a Stenvale Aria 2. I was glad to have it, but its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I finished the day with a legal pad propping it up. I reported that to Gloria in my battery approval email. She acknowledged it in the pickup email and said they would repair the arm. I cannot say whether that repair has since been done.

The phone situation is the real weakness. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day. Her email referred to a voicemail from her, but that does not change the difficulty of reaching the shop or leaving a message when I called.

Their stated phone hours are Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. For anyone working a Monday docket, that is a significant limitation, not just a minor inconvenience. I would plan around those hours and use email rather than count on reaching someone by phone.

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road in Towson, with free parking in back. My experience was good technical work, a quicker-than-quoted turnaround and clear documentation, alongside a loaner problem and limited phone access.

Dana, based on this visit, I would trust Gloria with an Aria 3 for this work, and I would use the shop again. I would also make sure the loaner holds its position before leaving and settle communication expectations at drop-off. The repair earned my confidence; the phone arrangements did not.

Maureen
